project: TruthLens: Explainable Text-Based Fake News Classification
dataset: ISOT Fake News Dataset (True.csv and Fake.csv)
dataset_source: True.csv contains Reuters articles; Fake.csv contains articles from outlets described by the dataset maintainers as unreliable.
source_label_limitation: Labels are inherited from dataset file/source membership. They are not independent fact-checks of each claim, and the two classes have different publisher distributions.
input_features: cleaned title plus full article body
preprocessing: lowercase, remove URLs, replace punctuation, collapse whitespace
duplicate_policy: Remove exact duplicate cleaned title-and-body texts before splitting; remove conflicting duplicate texts if any are present.
split: stratified random split: 80% train, 20% held-out test
threshold_policy: UNCERTAIN is shown when the highest Logistic Regression class score is below the fixed application cutoff. Scores are not calibrated truth probabilities.
evaluation_note: These are held-out results for this cleaned, deduplicated ISOT split. ISOT's real articles are primarily from Reuters, while its fake articles come from other outlets; performance may reflect publisher, topic, or writing-style cues. Do not interpret these numbers as accuracy on arbitrary current news or as fact verification.
